MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, DECEMBER 6, 2021

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to

  teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR EDLER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Edler, Carman, Schachter, Scott, Yoo, Zigrang

  Commissioners Absent:  Medawar

  City Staff Present:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Also Present:  Donald M. Davis, City Attorney

   C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210382; ADDRESS: 7 Sorrel Lane, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Paul and Gina Pham; A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination (NC-210383) for one and two-story additions to be constructed
  along the front, side and rear yards of a two-story residence with a detached garage. A
  Minor Deviation (MD-210384) is required to for the construction of a single-story addition to
  be built along the existing easterly building line that encroaches into a side yard (4'-8"),
  where that side yard was legally established but nonconforming (10' min required). A
  second Minor Deviation (MD-210385) is required for the reduction of the front yard by less
  than 10%. A Variance (V-210386) is required for the encroachment of the proposed porch
  addition into the required front yard which projects beyond the forwardmost building line.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that some issues came up after the agenda had been posted
  that may require a change to the entitlements and re-noticing. Staff is requesting that this item be
  continued to the next Planning Commission meeting of Monday, January 10, 2022.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210382  TO  THE  PLANNING
  COMMISSION MEETING OF JANUARY 10, 2022.

  AYES:  EDLER, SCOTT, CARMAN, SCHACHTER, YOO, ZIGRANG
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  MEDAWAR
  ABSTAIN:

  CHAIR EDLER recused himself from Item 8A since he resides within 500’ of the subject site.

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210231; ADDRESS: 11 MONTECILLO DRIVE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: PETER SMITH ON BEHALF OF THE JACK
  KRAMER CLUB; DESCRIPTION: A request to approve a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-
  210232) to amend CUP-102-87, revising the parking requirement methodology to be
  consistent with current standards. There are no proposed expansions to existing facilities
  or programming schedules.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that there was a closed session regarding this item prior to this
  meeting. No actions or decisions were made and there are no actions to report.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that this item was continued from the Planning Commission
  meeting of November 1, 2021 to allow the applicant sufficient time to conduct outreach and
  meetings with the Montecillo and Casaba Estates Homeowners Associations.
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that all parties were able to come to a mutual agreement on a
  voluntary equity membership cap of 315 members. The membership cap is referenced in the CUP
  resolution and is part of the conditions of approval. The programming schedule and site plan, which
  notes that there are 66 parking spaces on the site, has been included as an attachment to the
  resolution. Staff has decoupled the site’s parking requirements from the membership cap as
  discussed at the November 1, 2021 Planning Commission meeting.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff received numerous emails and eComment
  correspondence from the Montecillo neighborhood. In discussions with the Montecillo HOA,
  correspondence was sent to residents prior to the staff report being posted on the current agenda
  on Friday, December 3, 2021. The issues that have been raised were addressed in the staff report
  and accompanying resolution. In addition, staff has worked with the City Attorney for more refined
  language to the conditions of approval, specifically addressing the membership cap in relation to
  the parking requirement. Planning Manager Naughton presented the redlined resolution and
  provided an overview of the changes that were made.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, continue
  the public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and adopt
  Resolution No. PA-210231, approving the request as conditioned.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  AYES:  SCOTT, CARMAN, SCHACHTER, YOO, ZIGRANG
  NOES:
  ABSTAIN:  EDLER
  ABSENT:  MEDAWAR

  Tahereh Barnes, JKC Board President, thanked the Planning Commission for considering their

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, DECEMBER 6, 2021
  2
   application. They held productive meetings with the homeowners association representatives and
  were able to come to a compromise that the club was willing to agree on.

  Peter Smith, General Manager, stated that the Jack Kramer Club and the homeowners association
  were able to have productive meetings and both parties are happy with the direction of the CUP.

  Howard Edelson, V.P. of Montecillo Homeowners Association, thanked the Planning
  Commissioners on behalf of the board and homeowners for allowing time for the homeowners
  association and the Jack Kramer Club to continue to have productive dialogue which resulted in
  an agreement for a 315 equity member cap and not an activity based approach. He also thanked
  the Jack Kramer Club, Dave Bradley, Peter Smith and Tahereh Barnes. Additionally, he thanked
  staff for reworking the staff report and resolution to reflect this agreement.

  Rudy Svorinich, Resident, stated that he is one of two property owners that border the Jack Kramer
  Club and thanked all involved for working with them to come up with this agreement which is
  reflected in the resolution. Mr. Svorinich requested a modification to general condition number 2
  that the following verbiage be added to state the following:

  “…upon notice of residents within 500’ of the Jack Kramer Club, and the homeowners association”.

  Mr. Svorinich stated that there is no issue with administrative approval but would like to be notified
  of what is being requested. He also requested a 30-day comment period.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked Mr. Smith and Ms. Barnes if they have any issue with the modification
  to the condition of approval requested by Mr. Svorinich. Mr. Smith and Ms. Barnes stated that they
  have no issue with the request.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked City Attorney Davis, if there is any issue with the modification to the
  condition of approval requested by Mr. Svorinich. City Attorney Davis stated that if the applicant
  has no issues, then he has no issues with the modification to the condition.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  AYES:  SCOTT, CARMAN, SCHACHTER, YOO, ZIGRANG
  NOES:
  ABSTAIN:  EDLER
  ABSENT:  MEDAWAR

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210231 AND ADOPT RESOLUTION NO.
  PA-210231 WITH STAFF’S AMENDMENTS AND THE MODIFICATION TO GENERAL
  CONDITION OF APPROVAL NO. 2.

  AYES:  SCOTT, CARMAN, SCHACHTER, YOO, ZIGRANG
  NOES:
  ABSTAIN:  EDLER
  ABSENT:  MEDAWAR

  B.  DRAFT GENERAL PLAN 2040 AND DRAFT PROGRAM ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT
  REPORT (PEIR)

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that there was a joint meeting in November with the Planning
  Commission and the City Council introducing the Draft General Plan and Draft Program
  Environmental Impact Report (PEIR). This is the first public hearing opening the draft document
  for deliberation.

  Planning Manager Naughton introduced Surabhi Barbhaya, John Bellas, and Dan Wery with
  Michael Baker International to present this item.

  Surabhi Barbhaya, Michael Baker International provided a presentation on the Draft General Plan.
  This included an overview of the eight elements, the Vision Statement, and 7 Guiding Principles.
  The notable changes to the General Plan were discussed including corrections and changes to
  land use designations.

  Dan Wery, Michael Baker International, provided a presentation on the Commercial District and
  the vision for the Commercial District.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, DECEMBER 6, 2021
  3
   John Bellas, Michael Baker International, provided a presentation on the Draft PEIR process and
  an overview of the topics studied in the PEIR. Three comment letters were received on the Draft
  PEIR from the LA County Fire Department, LA County Sanitation District, and the Metropolitan
  Water District. The LA County Fire Department had virtually no comments on the Draft EIR; the LA
  County Sanitation District made clarification to information they had provided during the Notice of
  Preparation process; and, the Metropolitan District wanted to clarify information about the Palos
  Verdes Reservoir and how it is described in the Draft PEIR and the Safety Element. These
  clarifications can be made in the final EIR process. Mr. Bellas provided an overview on the next
  steps.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, open
  the public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues related to the Draft General Plan and
  Draft PEIR; and continue the item to the January 10, 2022 Planning Commission meeting.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN inquired about the traffic study, which included traffic counts from
  2021 and asked how the reality of traffic is adapted, since school traffic was down due to COVID.
  Mr. Bellas stated that the traffic counts were taken in 2017 (pre-pandemic); those counts were
  updated with growth data on an annual basis.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that in the mobility section (Section 3-16) there is mention of
  potential widening of some streets and this may be a concern to the community; the problem seems
  to be understated. Mr. Bellas stated that he understands that traffic is congested during peak hours
  on Palos Verdes Drive North (PVDN). Mr. Bellas stated that the General Plan Update does not
  include the expansion of lanes on PVDN and it would remain a 2-lane roadway going each way. In
  this section PVDN is under the classification of a 2 to 4 lane roadway, but it is understood that
  PVDN is a 2-lane roadway. Ms. Barbhaya stated that a future project is to develop design
  guidelines for the scenic corridor roadways in the city.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that there was some conversation on how high buildings in the
  Commercial District could be, to preserve visibility of the surrounding topography.
  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that the mention of three- or four-story buildings is vague and
  would like to make sure that the floor area does not come out to the street and reduce the visibility
  to the canyon. Mr. Bellas stated that the floor area ratio (FAR) is 2.5 for the commercial district,
  which means that you can have 2.5 times your land size in building square footage; if the parcel is
  entirely built out, then the building could be taller in some places. Mr. Wery stated that he is
  suggesting to maintain the current height and setback requirements and potentially incentivize or
  require step-backs; as you get to the upper levels, there would be a deck or terrace before getting
  to the vertical story. The massing or volume will be decreased from 3 times the lot area to 2.5 times
  the lot area. If the Promenade Mall were to be reconfigured or redeveloped, then it would be
  reduced in height by approximately 20 to 25 feet.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that everyone involved put a lot of thought into what would
  happen with the Commercial District as a multi-use area and hopefully to revitalize it. When projects
  are presented, they should be considered in their entirety and not just looked at as individual
  buildings.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked how FAR treats parking lots or parking structures. Mr. Bellas stated
  typically when parking lots are wrapped, hidden or underground, they are not counted as floor area.
  Director Wahba stated that parking lots are not typically counted in the FAR, but this is something
  that could be considered since it creates volume.

  Director Wahba stated that the form-based code concept that was discussed would help regulate
  the setbacks and height of buildings and how they step away from the street.
  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that if the parking is underneath the building, you don’t get the benefits
  if it is not counted as FAR. Mr. Wery stated that the FAR is the permissible habitable, leasable, or
  active space that generates uses. The dimensional standards would be used to regulate massing.
  If there is parking underneath, the building cannot be higher than what is allowed; the building
  would need to fit in to the height limits.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked about how traffic is factored in with the development of Deep Valley
  Drive, potential redevelopment of Silver Spur Road, and the reduction of number of lanes on Silver
  Spur Road. Mr. Bellas stated that the conclusion of the traffic study showed that there is an increase
  in trip generation in the Commercial District due to the increase in residential units. Mr. Bellas
  stated that they are anticipating a decrease in active commercial square footage in the Commercial

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, DECEMBER 6, 2021
  4
   District due to trends and market studies, with less reliance on brick and mortar retail and office
  space, due to people transitioning to remote working. This coupled with the overdeveloped level
  on Silver Spur Road, could support a reduction of lanes to create a more “main street” feeling.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked how much reduction of commercial space is expected. Mr. Bellas
  stated that in the next 20 years, it is expected that there would be 9 - 20% reduction in commercial
  square footage. COMMISSIONER YOO asked how much increase in residential use is expected.
  Mr. Bellas stated that on the low end, 900 new residential units and on the high end, 1400 new
  residential units are projected.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked for clarification on how the increase in density would not impact
  traffic. Mr. Bellas explained that there is allowable use, which currently is 22 units per acre, and
  the actual use. It is recommended that the allowable use increase to 30 units per acre. Market
  studies have shown and developers have expressed to the city, that it is difficult to build a multi-
  residential product in the Commercial District due to the high land cost. The residential market is
  likely going to drive development and redevelopment in the Commercial District. To incentivize
  some growth in the Commercial District, it makes sense to increase the allowable density. Ms.
  Barbhaya added that one of the things that was looked at was what each of the land uses produce
  in terms of traffic. According to the ITE Manual, retail uses produce five to seven times the traffic
  compared to residential uses.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT commented that going from 22 units per acre to 30 units per acre just inflates
  the price of property and expressed his concern with densifying a city that may not be able to
  evacuate in case of an emergency. Mr. Bellas stated that what the market research shows and
  what developers have expressed is that even at 30 units per acre, it is difficult to build multi-
  residential products in the city. Mr. Bellas stated that evacuating in emergencies is something that
  they continue to look at. There have been two fires, one in 1973 and one in 2009 and both primarily
  burned the Portuguese Bend area; and in both instances approximately 1,200 residents were
  evacuated. Mr. Bellas stated that he does not discount that more evacuations could be necessary
  in an emergency situation.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT expressed his concern with traffic on PVDN and stated that adding multi-unit
  residential is going to make it worse and believes that what is being proposed is not a good idea.
  Mr. Bellas stated that all recommendations have been discussed at the General Plan Advisory
  Committee level, General Plan Subcommittee level, staff level, and through community outreach
  campaigns. The synthesis was to have a thriving Commercial District for people of all generations.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked if their studies showed that there would be any demand for commercial
  development or will every turnover of a building go to residential. Mr. Bellas stated that commercial
  uses in the Commercial District are antiquated and what is becoming more desirable is the
  experience; restaurants are a more desirable and profitable use.

  Director Wahba stated that 30 units per acre is a modest number and at one point, the study was
  indicating that the city would need to be at 90 to 100 units per acre. In order for a developer to go
  higher, concessions would need to be made to provide something to the community, such as an
  outdoor plaza space. There need to be creative ways to entice developers to come up and
  redevelop. The hope is that as more people reside in the commercial district, they will not all be
  driving.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked about workforce housing on school campuses and asked if only
  school district employees can buy properties. Ms. Barbhaya stated that the idea is that these will
  be rental properties for school district employees. Planning Manager Naughton added that there
  would be opportunity to restrict those units to school district employees, however, they can also be
  made available to people who work on the Peninsula and are not school district employees.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CONTINUE THIS ITEM TO THE JANUARY 10, 2022 PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT requested an update on 9 Lantana. Director Wahba stated that the contractor
  said that he will start working in the next couple of days.

  CHAIR EDLER asked about the landscape along the view corridor on the berm at Casaba and

  5
   PVDN. Director Wahba apologized and stated that he will work on this.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN thanked VICE CHAIR SCOTT for his public service within the
  community for over 22 years as a Planning Commissioner and HOA President and stated that he
  definitely left his mark on the community with his wisdom and expertise.
  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that he was asked to attend a meeting in 1996 and shortly thereafter
  became president of the homeowners’ association. He joined the Planning Commission when Larry
  Vanden Bos stepped up to the school board. He expressed his appreciation for staff’s work and
  service to the Planning Commission and to the city. He thanked the Planning Commissioners for
  several years of good fun here.

  10.  MANAGER ITEMS

  Director Wahba stated that the City Council will hold a special meeting tomorrow, Tuesday,
  December 7, 2021 where five candidates for the Planning Commission will be interviewed.

  Planning Manager Naughton recognized VICE CHAIR SCOTT and read a brief statement on his
  accomplishments while serving on the Planning Commission. VICE CHAIR SCOTT will be formally
  recognized at the January 25, 2022 City Council meeting. Planning Manager Naughton thanked
  VICE CHAIR SCOTT for his dedicated service, engagement, participation, and astute insight on
  difficult land use issues and for always being an advocate for his community.
